26 A surveyor’s device emits a pulse of light. The light is reflected from a wall 150 m away.
What is the time taken for the pulse to travel from the device to the wall and then back to the
device?
A
0.05 ns
B
0.10 ns
C
0.50 µs
D
1.0 µs

hints: Notice the wording to the wall and then back - the $150 \text{ m}$ one-way distance must be doubled to $300 \text{ m}$ total path.
Connect the light pulse to its speed in air, $c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and use $t = d/v$.
Compare your time in seconds with $10^{-6} \text{ s} = 1.0 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$ and $10^{-9} \text{ s} = 1.0 \text{ ns}$ to choose the correct prefix.
walkthrough: Identify the total distance. One way is $150 \text{ m}$, so device to wall and back is $d = 2 \times 150 \text{ m} = 300 \text{ m}$.
State the governing rule. For a light pulse, speed $v \approx c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = d/t$, so $t = d/c$.
Substitute values with units: $t = 300 \text{ m} / 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 1.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s}$.
Check units and prefix. $10^{-6} \text{ s}$ is $1.0 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$, while $\text{ns}$ means $10^{-9} \text{ s}$ and would be far too short.
The $1.0 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$ result matches the $300 \text{ m}$ round trip. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 20000. It ignores the $300 \text{ m}$ round trip and confuses $\text{ns}$ with $\mu\text{s}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 10000. A time in $\text{ns}$ would only allow light to travel a few centimetres, not to a $150 \text{ m}$ wall and back.

C.explanation: This is half the correct time. It uses only the one-way $150 \text{ m}$ distance instead of the $300 \text{ m}$ go-and-return distance.

D.explanation: Total distance $300 \text{ m}$ at $c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives $t = 1.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s} = 1.0 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$.
